text: {"features":[{"name":"Role alignment","description":"How clearly the letter connects the candidate's interests and prior work to the specific goals of Google's Information Security Engineering role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter expresses interest in security or backend work in broad terms, with little tailoring to Information Security Engineering or Google's stated mission."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter names the team or mission and gives a plausible reason for applying, but the rationale stays fairly generic."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter connects the application to at least one specific part of the role, such as secure-by-default tooling, vulnerability response, or security automation."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter links several duties from the posting to the candidate's own background and explains why this role is a logical next step."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter delivers a highly targeted case for this exact role by weaving the team's mandate, the candidate's past work, and the impact they want to have into one coherent rationale."}]},{"name":"Software track record","description":"How strong the evidence is of professional experience testing, maintaining, and launching production software.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter presents the low end of experience seen here, such as roughly three years of work and responsibility for only a couple of production services."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter shows either somewhat more time or somewhat more delivery scope, but still with a modest production record overall."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows a solid midrange track record, such as three to five years with repeated testing, maintenance, and launch responsibility across several services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong production experience through either longer tenure or broader service ownership, such as four to six services or equivalent repeated delivery."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter combines extended experience with substantial production scope, matching the strongest cases here through roughly five to seven years and repeated launch or maintenance of many services."}]},{"name":"Go depth","description":"How convincingly the letter establishes substantial Go experience relevant to backend or infrastructure work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter states that Go is a main language but gives no additional context about what was built with it or why that matters here."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter identifies Go as a regular production language and lightly connects it to the candidate's background."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly presents Go as a main working language in recent production systems."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter ties Go directly to meaningful backend or infrastructure ownership relevant to security tooling."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes Go central to the candidate's fit by linking it to backend systems or guardrail infrastructure that closely mirror the role's responsibilities."}]},{"name":"Python depth","description":"How convincingly the letter establishes substantive Python experience for tooling, automation, or agent work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter omits Python or mentions it so vaguely that real working ability cannot be inferred."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter indicates some Python use but mainly as incidental scripting or a secondary tool."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows regular Python use for services, automation, tooling, or analysis in professional settings."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong Python ownership across multiple uses such as services, tooling, data pipelines, analysis, or test infrastructure."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents Python as a production-grade strength that is directly relevant to automation, agents, or analysis layers in this role."}]},{"name":"Agentic design","description":"How much concrete experience the letter shows designing agents and the surrounding control infrastructure.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter does not mention agents or describes automation without any agent-specific architecture."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions agentic systems but gives little detail about components, constraints, or the applicant's role in building them."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows direct involvement in agent-based systems and identifies both the agents and the surrounding services or infrastructure."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes designing agentic systems with concrete control mechanisms such as contracts, permissions, audit logs, or bounded actions."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, positioning safe agent design plus its guardrail infrastructure as a major strength."}]},{"name":"Vulnerability automation","description":"How much direct experience the letter shows automating vulnerability intake, triage, routing, deduplication, or variant analysis.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no direct evidence of automating vulnerability handling."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter refers to vulnerability response or queue work in general terms without explaining what was automated."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly states that the candidate built tooling for vulnerability triage, intake, or routing."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter adds concrete functions such as classification, deduplication, owner assignment, or clear reduction of manual effort."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents vulnerability automation as a sophisticated systems effort, describing a robust pipeline that makes handling reports structured, routed, and largely self-serve or scalable."}]},{"name":"Security assessments","description":"How much concrete experience the letter shows performing security assessments of systems or code.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no direct evidence of having performed security assessments."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter implies some security review exposure but without naming methods or scope."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states hands-on assessment work and names at least one recognizable activity such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, or validating fixes."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows structured assessment experience across multiple contexts, such as both new designs and existing services, with follow-through on remediation."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents security assessment as a substantial practice, emphasizing repeated rigorous reviews carried out with an attacker's mindset and verified remediation."}]},{"name":"AI application","description":"How much concrete experience the letter shows building, shipping, or evaluating AI-powered features in production.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of AI or LLM experience."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions AI interest or superficial exposure without showing shipped work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states direct experience building or shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter adds production discipline by mentioning evaluation, reliability work, safeguards, or explicit handling of failure modes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents applied AI as a strong competency by pairing shipped model-based systems with clear evidence of making them dependable in production."}]},{"name":"Algorithmic fluency","description":"How well the letter evidences practical use of data structures and algorithms to improve real systems.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter offers no concrete evidence of data structures or algorithms work beyond a generic claim."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter claims strength in algorithms but gives little or no example of real application."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter provides a clear applied example such as redesigning scheduling, lookup, indexing, matching, deduplication, or correlation logic."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter uses the example to show meaningful technical improvement such as better tractability, performance, or reduced bugs."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows especially strong practical fluency through a substantial algorithmic redesign that solved a previously hard or high-impact system problem in a memorable way."}]},{"name":"Developer enablement","description":"How clearly the letter frames security engineering as helping other engineers move faster and more safely.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter says little about helping other engineers or reducing friction for them."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter gestures at secure development or automation but does not clearly frame the work as enabling others."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter explicitly talks about making secure behavior easier or reducing manual toil for developers or security teams."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter repeatedly frames impact as removing friction, returning expert time, or making the right path the easy path for busy engineers."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes enablement a defining theme, treating security tooling as a way to embed good defaults and scale expert judgment without burdening product teams."}]},{"name":"Platform leverage","description":"How well the letter demonstrates understanding of the role's company-wide leverage and foundational infrastructure impact.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter shows little awareness of why this work matters at an organization-wide or foundational level."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions scale or impact in broad terms but does not explain the multiplier effect of central security tooling."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly connects the role to foundational systems or company-wide reach."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong understanding of central platform work by describing multiplier effects across many teams or services."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter articulates platform leverage in especially thoughtful terms, treating this role as capacity-building infrastructure whose benefits compound across the organization."}]},{"name":"Collaboration orientation","description":"How clearly the letter indicates readiness to work with security specialists and internal users of the tooling.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter does not mention working with security specialists or internal users of the tooling."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions teams generically without showing how collaboration shapes the work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter indicates comfort working alongside security engineers or building close to the developers who use the tools."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter emphasizes collaboration or user proximity as an important part of building effective security systems."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes cross-functional partnership central to the case, showing the candidate as someone who builds better systems through close work with security experts and internal engineering customers."}]},{"name":"Security depth","description":"How much extra evidence the letter provides of security seriousness outside ordinary product engineering duties.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter provides no extra evidence of security seriousness beyond ordinary software experience."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter adds a light signal such as occasional CTFs, a basic certification, or brief attacker-minded language."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter gives a clear extra signal through regular CTF participation, a recognized certification, or sustained offensive-security framing."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter offers strong extra credibility through demanding signals such as OSCP or high-level competition results."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter combines high-signal security practice with language that clearly reflects disciplined offensive intuition or sustained security study."}]},{"name":"Technical initiative","description":"How much the letter shows self-directed engineering beyond assigned job scope through open source, upstream work, or personal builds.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter shows little or no self-directed engineering beyond assigned work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions a small side build or occasional upstream contribution without showing sustained ownership."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter provides one clear example of initiative, such as maintaining an open-source project, sending upstream fixes, or finishing a personal project."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows sustained initiative through meaningful open-source maintenance or a technically substantive personal system."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows exceptional initiative through widely used open source, ambitious independent systems work, or both."}]},{"name":"Security rigor","description":"How strongly the letter conveys a mindset of building safe, constrained, dependable systems suited to security work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives little indication of building systems with security-specific care, constraints, or reliability concerns."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter hints at seriousness or quality standards but without concrete language about safe or dependable design."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly expresses a preference for trustworthy systems and mentions at least one concrete control idea such as boundaries, testing, audits, or correctness."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter repeatedly emphasizes constrained, reliable, or auditable engineering in ways tied to past work."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes dependable security-minded engineering a defining theme, showing systems built around strong boundaries, auditability, and production trustworthiness."}]},{"name":"Evidence strength","description":"How concrete and verifiable the letter's claims are through details, examples, and observable outcomes.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter relies mostly on generic claims or buzzwords, with few details that let a reader verify what the candidate actually did."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter includes some concrete tasks or technologies but leaves many important claims thinly supported."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter regularly grounds claims in identifiable technologies, architectures, examples, or responsibilities."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter supports most claims with tangible detail such as specific functions, operational effects, or clear ownership language."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes the case through dense, precise evidence, so the candidate's contribution and impact are easy to picture and trust."}]},{"name":"Organization","description":"How clearly and logically the letter presents its argument for fit from opening through closing.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter reads as disjointed enough that the main case for fit is hard to follow."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter has a basic structure but moves between points somewhat abruptly or unevenly."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter follows a clear and readable progression from background to fit."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter is well organized, with paragraphs that each serve a distinct purpose and reinforce the application's logic."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter feels tightly constructed, with a deliberate flow that turns separate facts into a cumulative argument for this role."}]},{"name":"Writing mechanics","description":"How polished the letter is at the sentence level in spelling, grammar, and proofreading.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter contains frequent spelling, grammar, or proofreading errors that repeatedly distract from the content."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter has several noticeable errors or awkward constructions but remains understandable."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter has occasional minor slips that do not materially interfere with readability."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter is clean and professional with only rare trivial mistakes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter is polished and essentially error-free throughout."}]}]}
